themes_detail.label: Illegal Dumping Surge
themes_detail.summary: Illegal dumping complaints spiked to 25 THIS WEEK versus a baseline average of 7.2 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 245% increase (z-score: 6.02)—suggesting either a new dumping operation or enforcement gap in Sunnyside/Woodside.
evidence: 25 illegal dumping complaints THIS WEEK vs. 7.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (245% spike)
Z-score of 6.02 indicates statistically significant anomaly
High severity rating in data; suggests concentrated incident or pattern
reporting_angles: Map the 25 complaints geographically this week—are they clustered on specific blocks or near a particular site?
Interview DSNY about enforcement response and whether they've identified a dumping hot spot or illegal carter operation

themes_detail.label: Panhandling Crisis Emerging
themes_detail.summary: Panhandling complaints exploded to 3 THIS WEEK from a baseline of 0.1 per week—a 2300% spike (z-score: 8.69)—marking an abrupt emergence of street-level homelessness or economic distress in the district.
evidence: 3 panhandling complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average (2300% spike)
Z-score of 8.69 indicates extreme statistical significance
New phenomenon: essentially zero complaints for 8 weeks, then sudden emergence
reporting_angles: Where are the 3 complaints concentrated? (Transit hubs, commercial strips, residential areas?) Interview complainants and local business owners.
Talk to Sunnyside/Woodside social services, shelters, and advocacy groups: Has there been a recent service closure, policy change, or influx of unhoused people?

themes_detail.label: Street Vendor Enforcement Spike
themes_detail.summary: Vendor enforcement complaints surged to 5 THIS WEEK versus 0.6 per week average—a 700% increase (z-score: 5.11)—suggesting either a new enforcement blitz or emerging illegal vending operations in Sunnyside/Woodside.
evidence: 5 vendor enforcement complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.6 weekly average (700% spike)
Z-score of 5.11 indicates high statistical significance
Aligns with outdoor dining spike last week (4 complaints vs. 0.4 avg, 967% increase)
reporting_angles: Has the city launched a new street vending enforcement campaign in CD 402 this week? Check with DCA and DOS.
Interview street vendors and business improvement districts: Are there illegal carts competing with licensed vendors, or is this about outdoor dining permit disputes?

themes_detail.label: Outdoor Dining Complaints Rise
themes_detail.summary: Outdoor dining complaints jumped to 4 LAST WEEK from a baseline of 0.4 per week—a 967% increase (z-score: 7.49)—indicating resident friction over seating, blockages, or sidewalk encroachment tied to ongoing outdoor dining expansion.
evidence: 4 outdoor dining complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly average (967% spike)
Z-score of 7.49 indicates high statistical significance
Concurrent spike in vendor enforcement (5 complaints THIS WEEK) suggests related street-use tension
reporting_angles: Walk Queens Boulevard and Greenpoint Avenue: How many outdoor dining sheds are operational? Are they blocking pedestrian or vehicle flow?
Interview community board members and residents: Is the issue unlicensed sheds, expired permits, or poor placement of licensed venues?

themes_detail.label: Food Safety Complaints Accelerate
themes_detail.summary: Food establishment complaints jumped to 8 LAST WEEK versus a baseline of 2.5 per week—a 220% increase (z-score: 4.92)—suggesting emerging health code violations or new restaurant/street food activity in Sunnyside/Woodside.
evidence: 8 food establishment complaints LAST WEEK vs. 2.5 weekly average (220% spike)
Z-score of 4.92 indicates high statistical significance
Overlaps with outdoor dining and vendor enforcement spikes, suggesting restaurant/food sector activity surge
reporting_angles: Request DOHMH violation data for the district last week: What were the 8 violations? (Pest activity, temperature control, cleanliness, licensing?)
Identify which establishments generated complaints; interview inspectors about whether this is a seasonal spike or new problem.
